To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the homogenization procedure can be used to compute effective elastic properties of woven or knitted textile materials with a periodic microstructure.
the effective in-plane behaviour of textile materials with multiple micro-contact is computed by the proposed algorithm.

the effective behaviour of textile-like materials with multiple periodic micro-contact is computed via the periodic unfolding strategy; the obtained results can be implemented for some specific textiles; the results are illustrated by simulation of woven and knit textiles.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the homogenization of periodic elastic structures with micro-contact.
the derivation of a homogenization algorithm for the effective in-plane behaviour of textile-like materials with multiple micro-contact.
the homogenization of periodic heterogeneous elastic bodies with frictional contact.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the homogenization method is a powerful tool for the prediction of the mechanical behaviour of textile materials.

, in the case of textile structures with multiple contact, the homogenized model is able to capture the main features of the microstructure and to predict the overall behaviour of the material with sufficient accuracy.
the proposed approach allows for a very efficient and accurate simulation of the macroscopic in-plane behaviour of woven and knited textiles.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the homogenized limit of a periodic problem with multiple contact can be obtained by the asymptotic analysis and unfolding method and the homogenized stress–strain relation can be computed by solving the contact problem in the representative volume element.
we have obtained a new effective model for textile materials, which is capable to describe the in-plane behaviour of textile-like materials, including the effect of multiple contact.
the effective in-plane behaviour of textile-like materials can be accurately computed by the homogenized limit, which is obtained by the periodic unfolding strategy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effective behaviour of textile-like materials can be computed by solving a non-linear contact problem on the representative volume element.
the homogenized model of textile materials with micro-contact can be computed efficiently by a two-scale algorithm.
the effective behaviour of textile-like materials is highly non-linear.
